simple.meaning: נָפָה (nâphâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a sieve.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: נָפָה (H5299) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Joshua 11:2, with occurrences in Joshua, 1 Kings, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָפָה (H5299) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in נָפָה (H5299) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: נָפָה (nâphâh) / H5299 is traced through Joshua 11:2, Joshua 12:23, 1 Kings 4:11, Isaiah 30:28 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

timeline.evidenceText: and to the kings who were on the north, in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, in the lowland, and in the heights of Dor on the west,
the king of Dor in the height of Dor, one;
Ben Abinadab, in all the height of Dor (he had Taphath, Solomon’s daughter, as wife);
His breath is as an overflowing stream that reaches even to the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of destruction. A bridle that leads to ruin will be in the jaws of the peoples.

definitions.full: H5299. naphah I. [ נָפָה ] noun feminine sieve or other winnowing implement, Di Du Schwinge , Che Hpt fan (as swung ); — only construct שָׁוְא בְּנָ֫פַת גוֺיִם לַהֲנָפָה Isa 30:28 to swing nations in a sieve of worthlessness. II. [ נָפָה ] noun feminine height ; — only construct in combination דּוֺר נָפַת Josh 12:23 = ׳נ דּאֹר 1Kin 4:11 , plural construct ד ׳נָפוֺת Josh 11:2 ; compare II. דּוֺד , and Di 11:2 ; see also [ נֶפֶת ].
